paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Paul says the old covenant, the ministry of death engraved on stone, came with real glory (2 Corinthians 3:7). But the glory of the Spirit, the ministry of righteousness, is so much greater that what was once glorious has "no glory now in comparison to the glory that surpasses it" (2 Corinthians 3:10). Moses' glory was fading. This glory endures (2 Corinthians 3:11).

So why does that matter to YOU? Because Paul says a veil covers hearts when Moses is read, but "whenever anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away" (2 Corinthians 3:15-16). Not after you clean up your act. Not after a hundred good days in a row. You turn, and the veil comes off. Honestly, I spent years in the dark waiting on somebody else to lift my cover, so this one gets me.

And look where Paul lands: "where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom" (2 Corinthians 3:17). With unveiled faces, we "are being transformed into His image with intensifying glory, which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit" (2 Corinthians 3:18). You aren't hiding, and you aren't running on a battery that's about to die. Turn to the Lord, baker, and keep your face lifted, because He's the one doing the changing.
